title: Template Tags: Logic in Templates
description: Use `if`, `for`, `block`, and other tags to control the output.

slides.title: Template Tags: {% ... %}
slides.content:
Tags are used for control structures, loops, and includes. They are enclosed in `{% %}`.

Common tags:
- `{% if condition %} ... {% endif %}`
- `{% for item in list %} ... {% endfor %}`
- `{% block name %} ... {% endblock %}`
- `{% include "file.html" %}`

slides.title: Conditionals
Loops
slides.content:
{% for post in posts %}
  • {{ forloop.counter }}: {{ post.title }}
    • {% if forloop.last %}
  • This is the last post.
    • {% endif %} {% empty %}
  • No posts yet.
    • {% endfor %}
The `forloop` object gives you `.counter`, `.first`, `.last`, etc.

quizData.question: What does the `{% empty %}` tag do inside a `{% for %}` loop?

options.text: It's used to end the loop
It provides content when the iterable is empty

quizData.explanation: `{% empty %}` is a clause of `{% for %}` that renders if the iterable has no items.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `forloop.parentloop` for nested loops

When you have loops inside loops, `forloop.parentloop` gives you access to the outer loop's counter.
